_comment: THE CAMPAIGN'S MACHINE REGISTRY -- one entry per participant, frozen 2026-08-05.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  --machine k was passed by hand on every launch, and a
typo there is the worst failure the harness has: two machines silently claim
the same rows and leave a hole somewhere else, which shows up at merge time
as 'rows MISSING' -- indistinguishable from a machine that never reported.
Detection removes the hand-typed index.
DETECTION FAILS LOUDLY, NEVER GUESSES.  An unrecognised host is an error, not
a default, for exactly the reason above.  To bring a new host online, run
python run_ensemble.py --register <index>
which appends this host's fingerprint to the matching entry.
WHY NOT HOSTNAME ALONE.  platform.node() on the Macs returns the DHCP name
'Mac.san.rr.com', and the v2 pool shows TWO PHYSICALLY DIFFERENT Macs (16-core
and 8-core) reporting that same string.  Hostname is matched only where it is
actually distinctive; the Macs are pinned on hw.model + core count as well.
WEIGHTS ARE FROZEN.  Changing a weight re-partitions the design, so rows
already computed change owner and get recomputed by somebody else.  Do not
edit `weight` mid-campaign; add capacity with --subtask instead.
SPEED PROVENANCE -- measured unless stated:
0 MacBook Pro   1.000  reference. 3780 s/row mean at the rev-6 grid,
1 Matrix-PC     0.400  DECLARED. Its manifest never arrived; the v2 pool
gives 2.7x-15x slower depending on how it is read.
2 Workstation   0.500  DECLARED by the author 2026-08-05. Never contributed
a row. Replace with a measurement when it has.
3 Hoffman2      0.214  measured: job 14223957 ran the reference row in
26059.6 s against the Mac's 5580.6 s, observables
matching to printed precision (plan S12(r)).

machines.name: MacBook Air
machines._note: Replaces Hoffman2, withdrawn 2026-08-05 after every row failed on its COMPUTE nodes at the production grid (TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable, 5-8 s per row). CAUSE NARROWED, NOT FOUND -- and NOT memory: a follow-up job on node n1032 ran the SAME row (59) at the SAME grid (I=30000/V=5000) to rc=0 with peak RSS 161 MB, ulimit -v unlimited and 16 G granted. What differs is the CALL PATH: that row succeeded through a direct RE.evaluate(), while the array job goes through run_ensemble's multiprocessing pool (--workers 4). The same pool path also worked on a compute node at I=300/V=480, so it is the combination of the pool and the production grid. Linux uses fork() where macOS uses spawn, and cpp_bridge drains solver stdout on threads -- fork+threads is the obvious suspect and is UNVERIFIED. *** THIS MAY ALSO AFFECT ANY LINUX PARTICIPANT, including machine 2. Before trusting a Linux machine's rows, run it with --limit 2 and confirm the rows take ~1 h, not seconds. hoffman2_array.sh and hoffman2_setup.sh are retained. With no registry entry, running on Hoffman2 fails detection loudly. MacBook Air speed 0.85 is DECLARED and deliberately below its burst figure: the Air is fanless and this is a 30+ h all-core load. Measure it from the first manifest; do NOT edit the weight mid-campaign -- that repartitions the design.
